{{nihongo|'''Ogawa Shrine'''|小川神社}} is a shrine located at Oneyama 6862, {{ill|Ogawa, Nagano|ceb|Ogawa Mura|de|Ogawa (Nagano)|es|Ogawa (Nagano)|fa|اوگاوا، ناگانو|fi|Ogawa|fr|Ogawa (Nagano)|hy|Օգավա (գյուղ)|it|Ogawa (Nagano)|ja|小川村|ko|오가와촌|my|အိုဂဝရွာ၊ နဂနို|ru|Огава (село)|th|โองาวะ (จังหวัดนางาโนะ)|tl|Ogawa, Nagano|tr|Ogawa, Nagano|uk|Оґава (Наґано)|ur|اوگاوا، ناگانو|uz|Ogava (Nagano)|zh|小川村|qid=Q1348971}}, {{ill|Kamiminochi District, Nagano|ceb|Kamiminochi-gun|de|Kamiminochi-gun|fi|Kami-Minochin piirikunta|fr|District de Kamiminochi|it|Distretto di Kamiminochi|ja|上水内郡|ko|가미미노치군|pl|Powiat Kamiminochi|uk|Повіт Камі-Міноті|zh|上水內郡|qid=Q1155074}}, {{ill|Nagano Prefecture|Q127877|qid=Q127877}}. It is a debated identification for a {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}} ronsha. It was formerly called Ōmiya Daimyōjin and Suwa Daimyōjingū<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>. {{nihongo|'''Ogawa Shrine'''|小川神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Shinano Province]].
== Overview ==
It was formerly known as Ōmiya Daimyōjin and Suwa Daimyōjingū. Shrine traditions and old records were lost in the {{ill|Meiwa|de|Meiwa|fa|میوا|fr|Ère Meiwa|it|Meiwa (era)|ja|明和|ko|메이와|ru|Мэйва|simple|Meiwa|sr|Меива|sv|Meiwa|tr|Meiwa|zh|明和|qid=Q1146161}} era. In addition, in {{ill|1933|Q18726|qid=Q18726}} (Shōwa 8), a fire at the shrine household destroyed written materials and old documents, including a permit issued by the {{ill|Yoshida family|fr|Clan Yoshida|ja|吉田家|ko|요시다가|simple|Yoshida family|qid=Q11413722}} in {{ill|1790|Q7775|qid=Q7775}} (Kansei 2). According to legend, the beginning was when Ogawa Mahito, a local magnate of Furuyama in Ogawa Village and a sake brewer, worshipped his ancestor {{ill|Emperor Keitai|Q349277|qid=Q349277|lt=Oto no Ōdo no Mikoto}} as the tutelary deity of Oneyama in Ogawa Village. Descendants of Ogawa Mahito built a fort at Furuyama and took the name Ogawa clan. In the {{ill|Kamakura period|Q236205|qid=Q236205}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ogawa Saemon Sadatsuna}} earned distinction in the {{ill|Jōkyū War|Q1372308|qid=Q1372308}}, became {{ill|Jitō|Q1329805|qid=Q1329805}} of {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ogawa-shō}}, ruled 3,000 koku of Ogawa-go as lord of {{ill|Ogawa Castle|Q11460417|qid=Q11460417}}, and repaired the shrine buildings. When the Ogawa clan was defeated in the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōnin War}}, the shrine buildings fell into ruin. Later, in {{ill|1536|Q6457|qid=Q6457}} (Tenbun 5), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ōhigata Danjō Masatada Kogorō Nagamasa}} came to rule Ogawa Village and the shrine was revived. The former shrine site was at Miyahira, on a hill next to the present site, known as a moon-viewing spot; when the Ōhigata clan developed the current site and moved the shrine there, only Oyama Shrine remained at the former site, and later that precinct land was used for school buildings and merged into this shrine. In {{ill|1598|Q6800|qid=Q6800}} (Keichō 3), when {{ill|Uesugi Kagekatsu|Q1376605|qid=Q1376605}} was transferred to {{ill|Aizu|Q1205071|qid=Q1205071}}, the {{ill|Ōhigata clan|Q11435635|qid=Q11435635}} also became {{ill|Rōnin|Q212418|qid=Q212418}} and settled locally, Furuyama Castle was abandoned, and the shrine household dispersed. In August {{ill|1790|Q7775|qid=Q7775}} (Kansei 2), the shrine petitioned the {{ill|Yoshida family|fr|Clan Yoshida|ja|吉田家|ko|요시다가|simple|Yoshida family|qid=Q11413722}} for an official declaration and, after receiving the notice, changed its name from Ōmiya Daimyōjin / Suwa Daimyōjingū to Ogawa Shrine. In January {{ill|1869|Q7720|qid=Q7720}} (Meiji 2), it became a prayer site of {{ill|Kachō-no-miya|Q11620129|qid=Q11620129}} and received imperial curtain and lantern items with the reverse chrysanthemum crest. In {{ill|1872|Q7753|qid=Q7753}} (Meiji 5), its 2-koku shrine estate was confiscated, and in June {{ill|1873|Q7757|qid=Q7757}} (Meiji 6) it was ranked as a village shrine, then promoted to gōsha on November 30, {{ill|1920|Q2155|qid=Q2155}} (Taishō 9)<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>.
The present main sanctuary was built in October {{ill|1729|Q6952|qid=Q6952}} (Kyōhō 14), and the roofed main hall plus heiden/haiden were newly rebuilt in {{ill|1956|Q5221|qid=Q5221}} (Shōwa 31)<ref>長野県上水内郡神社誌編纂委員会編『長野県上水内郡神社誌』（長野県神社庁上水内支部、1963年）202頁</ref>.
{{ill|Ogawa, Nagano|ceb|Ogawa Mura|de|Ogawa (Nagano)|es|Ogawa (Nagano)|fa|اوگاوا، ناگانو|fi|Ogawa|fr|Ogawa (Nagano)|hy|Օգավա (գյուղ)|it|Ogawa (Nagano)|ja|小川村|ko|오가와촌|my|အိုဂဝရွာ၊ နဂနို|ru|Огава (село)|th|โองาวะ (จังหวัดนางาโนะ)|tl|Ogawa, Nagano|tr|Ogawa, Nagano|uk|Оґава (Наґано)|ur|اوگاوا، ناگانو|uz|Ogava (Nagano)|zh|小川村|qid=Q1348971}} also has {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Sawanomiya Ogawa Shrine}}, another debated candidate for the {{ill|Shikinaisha|fr|Shikinaisha|zh|式內社|qid=Q134917286|lt=Shikinaisha}}. According to a document dated April {{ill|1768|Q7675|qid=Q7675}} (Meiwa 5), both Ogawa Shrines shared the same priest (Sakai Nagato), parishioners, and enshrined deity; although the order of their foundations is unknown, they are considered to have originally formed one unit as inner and outer shrine sites<ref>戸谷一郎『精説長野県史』123頁（日本精神文化研究所、1962年）</ref>.
